summary: An on/off switch for a setting, with its label, description and error laid out beside it, taking part in forms.

label.note: Visible label beside the track and the accessible name. Required: an external <label for> activates the host but does not name the inner control. States the setting, not the action ("Wi-Fi", not "Turn on Wi-Fi").

hideLabel.note: Visually hides the label; it stays the accessible name. Use only when other visible text in the row names the setting.

description.note: Help text under the label, read as the accessible description.

error.note: Error message under the label. Setting it marks the field invalid and blocks form submission (customError).

size.note: Track and thumb size: default 32x20 track with a 16px thumb; sm 24x16 track with a 12px thumb. Label text size does not change.

value.note: Submitted under name while the switch is on; nothing is submitted while it is off (like a native checkbox).

checked.note: On (true) or off (false). The property is the live state and is not reflected; the attribute is the default that form reset restores.

required.note: Native required: the switch must be on for the form to be valid (valueMissing while off). Adds an aria-hidden asterisk after the label.

disabled.note: Cannot be focused or toggled, dimmed, not submitted and skipped by validation. A disabled <fieldset> ancestor has the same effect without changing this attribute.

anatomy.name: field
anatomy.notes: Grid: the control in the first column; label, description and error in the second.

anatomy.name: control
anatomy.notes: Positions the track and thumb over the native input; vertically centered on the first line of the label.

anatomy.name: input
anatomy.notes: Native <input type="checkbox" role="switch">, visually covering the track; receives focus, Space, the checked state and validation.

anatomy.name: track
anatomy.notes: Pill-shaped track: off color while off, on color while on. Decorative (aria-hidden); the input carries the semantics.

anatomy.name: thumb
anatomy.notes: Round knob inset in the track: at the start edge while off, at the end edge while on (mirrored in right-to-left). Its position, not only color, shows the state.

anatomy.name: label
anatomy.notes: Native <label for> in the same shadow root; clicking it toggles the switch.

anatomy.name: error
anatomy.notes: Persistent polite live region; its text appears while invalid.

input.note: Each user toggle. Native and composed, so it crosses the shadow boundary.

change.note: Toggle committed by the user (not by setting checked from code). Re-dispatched from the host because native change is not composed; FormData read in the listener already has the new value.

hover.trigger: pointer over an enabled switch or its label

focus-visible.note: 3px solid ring around the track, offset from it so it stays visible against the on color (a translucent ring would fall under 3:1).

checked.note: Track takes the on color and the thumb moves to the end edge.

invalid.trigger: error set, or required and off after the user toggled it off, blurred it, or a submit attempt

disabled.trigger: disabled attribute or a disabled fieldset ancestor
disabled.note: Track, thumb and label dimmed; not-allowed cursor.

accessibility.accessibleNameSource: The label prop, through a native <label for> in the same shadow root.

formAssociation.note: ElementInternals: submits value under name only while on; validity mirrored from the inner input (required while off -> valueMissing; error -> customError); form reset restores the checked attribute; a disabled switch or one in a disabled fieldset is not submitted and not validated; form state restore re-applies the saved on/off state; <label for> on the host toggles it.

accessibility.targetSize: Track is 32x20 (default) or 24x16 (sm); the label beside it is part of the clickable area and the gap to the label satisfies the WCAG 2.5.8 spacing exception at both sizes.
accessibility.focusRingVisible: On keyboard focus of the input; 3px solid ring in switch.focus-ring.color, offset from the track.
accessibility.missingNameWarning: Dev-only console warning, once, when label is empty.

keyboard.Tab: moves focus to and from the switch (one tab stop)
keyboard.Shift+Tab: moves focus to the previous focusable element
keyboard.Enter: submits the form (implicit submission, as on a native checkbox; the inner control has no form owner in its shadow root, SB-0009); does not toggle

aria: role="switch" on the native checkbox input; aria-checked is exposed natively from its checked state (true/false, never mixed)
aria-describedby -> description and error ids (same shadow root)
required: native required on the input; the asterisk is aria-hidden
error: sets a customError validity, so the form blocks submission
track and thumb are aria-hidden decoration; the label text is never changed to on/off wording
announcements: the state is announced by the screen reader as on/off from role=switch on each toggle; the component adds no live text for it
error text is announced once when it appears (persistent aria-live=polite region)

useCases.when: A single setting that is either on or off, such as a preference in a settings form
useCases.use: sb-switch with a label naming the setting

useCases.when: The consequence of turning the setting on needs explaining
The setting must be on before the form can be submitted
useCases.use: required, with a label that states what is being enabled

useCases.when: A dense list or table row of settings
The row already has a visible heading naming the setting
useCases.use: hide-label, keeping label as the accessible name

antiPatterns.pattern: A switch for a choice that only takes effect after a separate confirm step, such as accepting terms
antiPatterns.why: A switch reads as a setting that is on or off right now; agreeing to something is a choice recorded on submit

antiPatterns.pattern: Choosing one of several options with a row of switches
antiPatterns.why: Switches are independent; nothing stops two from being on

antiPatterns.pattern: A label that names the action or changes with the state ("Turn on" / "Turn off")
antiPatterns.why: The switch role already announces on/off; a changing label contradicts it and confuses voice-control users
antiPatterns.alternative: A fixed label naming the setting

antiPatterns.why: A switch is only on or off (the switch role has no mixed value)

antiPatterns.pattern: A pressed/unpressed toolbar button styled as a switch
antiPatterns.why: A toggle button applies a formatting or view mode and is not a form field

drift.contract: label, description and error are props of Switch
drift.realization: shadcn composes Label and Field parts around Switch; shadow DOM requires them inside the component

drift.contract: 3px solid ring in color.ring, offset from the track
32x20 (default) and 24x16 (sm) from the size.switch tokens, thumb 16px / 12px inset 2px
drift.realization: shadcn uses 32x18.4 and 24x14 with a 1px transparent border; rounded to the 4px size scale

drift.contract: thumb color.background while off, color.primary-foreground while on, in every mode
drift.realization: shadcn switches the off thumb to foreground in dark mode; one semantic token per role keeps modes in the semantic layer
not reflected: the attribute is the default restored by form reset (shadcn/Radix reflects data-state)

drift.contract: invalid track border in color.destructive plus the error text
drift.realization: shadcn styles aria-invalid with a translucent destructive ring

openQuestions.question: Contract content drafted with the contract-author skill (visual reference, WAI-ARIA APG)?
openQuestions.answer: Yes: WAI-ARIA APG switch pattern (native checkbox with role=switch), the visual reference for look and sizes, Checkbox as the in-house form-control model.

openQuestions.question: Native <input type=checkbox role=switch>, or a <button role=switch aria-checked>?
openQuestions.answer: Native checkbox with role=switch: Space, checked state, required/valueMissing and the validation message come from the browser, and it reuses FormAssociated + NativeControl like Checkbox (SB-0007). The button variant would need hand-made keyboard, validity and state code.

openQuestions.question: Does Enter toggle the switch (APG lists it as optional)?
openQuestions.recommendation: No: Space toggles, Enter submits the form.
openQuestions.answer: No. Space toggles; Enter submits the form like every other form control in the library (SB-0009) and like a native checkbox. Toggling on Enter would make Enter in a settings form do two different things.

openQuestions.question: Is checked reflected to an attribute?
openQuestions.answer: No. The checked attribute is the default that form reset restores (like native defaultChecked); the property is the live state.

openQuestions.question: Is label required, and where does it sit?
openQuestions.recommendation: Required; after the track; hide-label for rows named elsewhere.
openQuestions.answer: Required, like Checkbox and Input; the label sits after the track (start side), as in the visual reference. hide-label keeps it as the name. No label-position prop until a real need appears (a settings row with the switch at the end is composed with Item).

openQuestions.question: Which sizes and what do they map to?
openQuestions.recommendation: default and sm, the visual reference's two sizes, on the existing size.switch tokens.
openQuestions.answer: size default (32x20 track, 16px thumb) and sm (24x16 track, 12px thumb), from the existing semantic tokens size.switch.* and space.switch.inset; spelled default/sm and mapped to the vocabulary's medium/small by the global size alias. No lg: the reference has none.

openQuestions.question: What does required mean for a switch?
openQuestions.recommendation: Must be on, as native required on a checkbox.
openQuestions.answer: The switch must be on (valueMissing while off), mirrored from the native input so the browser message and reportValidity() focus come for free. Invalid look shows after user interaction or a submit attempt, not on first render.

openQuestions.question: Does the thumb animate?
openQuestions.recommendation: Yes, a short slide, removed under prefers-reduced-motion.
openQuestions.answer: Thumb and track color transition over motion.duration.fast with motion.easing.standard; no transition when the user prefers reduced motion (WCAG 2.3.3).
